children: Bankers expect the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, with a majority also expecting the MPC to deliver a cumulative 50-75 bps rate hike by the end of FY27, according to a poll of bank economists conducted by businessline.

Eleven of the 12 chief economists from major public and private sector banks surveyed expect a 25-bps increase in the repo rate, taking it to 5.50 per cent. Only Bank of Baroda’s Chief Economist, Madan Sabnavis, expects the MPC to keep rates unchanged.

Seven out of 10 respondents expect the RBI to maintain a neutral policy stance. Two banks, DBS Bank and RBL Bank, anticipate a shift to a “withdrawal of accommodation” stance, while Sabnavis believes the central bank could adopt a more hawkish tone.

All respondents who forecast a rate hike cited rising inflation expectations, the need to align with global central bank actions, and concerns over imported inflation stemming from elevated crude oil prices as key reasons for their call.

“We believe that the start of a rate-hike cycle is warranted at the current juncture to align with global central banks, address rising inflation risks, and take advantage of strong domestic growth, which provides policy space for a cumulative 75 bps hike,” said Kanika Pasricha, Chief Economist at Union Bank of India.
Echoing a similar view, Gaura Sengupta, chief economist, IDFC First Bank said, “We expect a shallow rate-hiking cycle of 75 bps, driven by a rise in domestic inflation.”
Up to 75 bps hike by FY27

While most bankers expect the policy stance to remain neutral, six economists forecast that FY27 could end with the repo rate at 6 per cent, implying a cumulative increase of 75 bps from current levels.

“A gradual broadening of price pressures is likely to keep headline inflation above 5 per cent in the second half of FY27, narrowing the real rate buffer and reinforcing the need for a tighter policy bias,” said Radhika Rao of DBS Bank.
Apart from higher crude oil prices, managing the rupee’s depreciation is also a factor supporting the case for a rate hike, according to Anitha Rangan, Chief Economist at RBL Bank.
Festive season argues for status quo

While Sabnavis expects the MPC to hold rates in October, he believes a 25 bps hike is likely in the December policy review, followed by another 25 bps increase in February. This would take the terminal repo rate to 5.75 per cent by the end of FY27.
Sabnavis argued that an immediate rate hike may not effectively transmit to deposit rates during the festive season, when spending tends to remain elevated.
“One can wait for some time before increasing rates. By not raising rates now, bond yields could cool,” he said.

title: businessline poll: MPC seen raising rates by 25 bps this week; majority expect 50-75 bps tightening by FY27
